messages.subject: Repairable Systems Using Simmer
parts:
Has anyone used simmer for repairable systems simulation?


I am interested in developing a simulation for a repairable system (i.e., a personal computer) that has multiple subsystems with varying intensity functions, which the actions taken at the time of an event are actions such as: "Replace with new", "Replace with used", "Turn on", "Turn off", etc.

To keep things simple the repairable system of interest will be a series system with subsystems and components that have intensity functions that are either: Renewal processes or non homogenous processes.

Does such work already exist using simmer?

Thanks for any insight you can provide.

2018-01-16 21:43 GMT+01:00 <czah...@iastate.edu>:
> Has anyone used simmer for repairable systems simulation?
>
>
> I am interested in developing a simulation for a repairable system (i.e., a
> personal computer) that has multiple subsystems with varying intensity
> functions, which the actions taken at the time of an event are actions such
> as: "Replace with new", "Replace with used", "Turn on", "Turn off", etc.
>
> To keep things simple the repairable system of interest will be a series
> system with subsystems and components that have intensity functions that are
> either: Renewal processes or non homogenous processes.
>
> Does such work already exist using simmer?
>
> Thanks for any insight you can provide.

I'm not familiar with repairable systems, but I would model each
subsystem's lifetime as a trajectory. For example, the lifetime of a
generic "part" would be something like the following (not tested):

part <- trajectory() %>%
## time to power on the system
timeout(power_on) %>%
## subscribe to "system on/off" events
trap("system on") %>%
## if an off is received, wait for repair and start again
trap("system off",
handler = trajectory() %>%
wait() %>%
## back to timeout(power_on)
rollback(4)) %>%
## the system is working
timeout(working) %>%
## until this part fails and sends an off event
untrap(c("system off", "system on")) %>%
send("system off") %>%
## repairing
seize("repair") %>%
timeout(repairing) %>%
release("repair") %>%
## signal on and back to timeout(power_on)
send("system on") %>%
rollback(10)

where "power_on" could be a constant, and "working" and "repairing"
are whatever stochastic processes you want.

Regards,
Iñaki
